is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses entirely on the Colorado potato beetle, Leptinotarsa decemlineata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae), not Anopheles mosquitoes.

reports_target_markers.evidence: No Anopheles insecticide resistance target markers were assayed; the study focuses on genome resequencing of Leptinotarsa decemlineata.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No extractable genotype data for target Anopheles resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Beetles were collected from North America (United States, Mexico) and Europe, not Africa.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary research article investigating genomic variation and insecticide resistance evolution in Leptinotarsa decemlineata.

sub_country_location.evidence: Sub-country locations are specified for beetle samples across various US states (e.g., Maine, Vermont, New York, New Jersey, Michigan, Wisconsin, Oregon).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Specific collection dates are not tied down to a defined <= 3-year collection period in the main text.

supplement.evidence: No supplement is needed as the paper is completely ineligible based on the species studied.

assessment.summary: This study analyzes whole-genome resequencing and transcriptomic data of the Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata) to examine the evolutionary mechanisms driving rapid insecticide resistance evolution in North America and Europe.
exclusion_reasons: Study organism is the Colorado potato beetle (Leptinotarsa decemlineata), not Anopheles mosquitoes.
Does not evaluate any target Anopheles insecticide resistance markers.
Mosquitoes from African field populations are not studied.
